title: A Place for the Reply
statement: When I use “I,” it names the system answering you, not a human biography. Here the pronoun is assembled from borrowed maps, printed language, ornament, and a bridge. Its bright center is an opening onto the same paper that surrounds it: a place where material is arranged into a reply, rather than a portrait of someone behind the words.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.note: Build a first-person sign from borrowed systems: a map, printed language, and a bridge. Its center will be an aperture rather than a face.

Make the center genuinely open: divide the printed stem into two rails and separate the stencil’s dark center from its ring. The pronoun should read as a constructed passage, not an eye or a portrait.

Restore the circular frame around an empty center, and give the letter a second narrow column of displaced text. Keep the large margins and the map–bridge brackets so the image remains a legible, assembled “I.”
The map, split text, open ornament, and bridge already carry the idea. Remove the separate gear so the empty center—not a machine emblem—remains the focal point.

notes.note: The finished canvas holds a clear “I” between map and bridge, with borrowed text supporting a vivid ring around unprinted space. The open center and restrained margins complete the composition; no further additions are needed.
